text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert — tokenizer-preproc (prompt-muncher) pods in us-west-2 are reporting high CPU and OOMKills. Paging @jordan and #incidents.
jordan: Oncall here, looking now. Which service exactly?
nina: tokenizer-preproc (prompt-muncher) — we've got repeated OOMKilled and 5 pod restarts in the last 3m. Node CPU at 95-100% during spikes.
jordan: Confirming. From kubernetes events: some pods show OOMKilled and others show container exit 137. Traffic spike from a single client prefix hitting the preprocess queue.
sam: Can we throttle upstream at the LB/ingress? If it's a bad client burst, returning 429s temporarily is safest.
maria: Pulling logs from one of the crashed pods — pasting snippet:
```
[2026-02-20T14:12:02Z] prompt-muncher: processing batch size=64
[2026-02-20T14:12:02Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (python) score 987
[2026-02-20T14:12:02Z] oom-killer: Killed process 4123 (python) total-vm:3456784kB, anon-rss:2300000kB
```
This looks like a hotloop expanding memory during tokenization for very long prompts.
leo: Nodes with the pods are also at 90% CPU; we should avoid draining too many at once. Recommend: 1) Add ingress-level rate limit for offending client prefix 2) Temporarily scale up tokenizer-preproc to soak load 3) Reduce per-pod concurrency/batch size.
jordan: Agreed. I'll apply a quick rate-limit on the ingress for that client and scale replicas.
devops-bot: Suggestion: apply rate-limit via envoy: `kubectl patch configmap envoy-ratelimit -n prod --type merge -p '{"data":{"client-prefix-rl":"10r/s"}}'` (validate in staging first).
sam: If ingress patch is slow, we can also `kubectl set env deployment/tokenizer-preproc --containers=tokenizer --env="TOKENIZER_MAX_BATCH=16"` to force smaller batches live.
maria: Applying small-batch env var now to deployment/tokenizer-preproc. Pushing rolling update (1m).
[system] deployment/tokenizer-preproc rollout started
jordan: Scaling replicas from 6 -> 12 to buy time: `kubectl scale deploy/tokenizer-preproc --replicas=12 -n prod`
leo: Watch node CPU — if pods just replicate hotloops we'll saturate the whole pool. I recommend also cordoning the node with most evictions as temporary stop-gap.
sam: For cordon: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-33` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data ip-10-0-45-33` — but be careful, draining will reschedule and might push load to other nodes.
maria: Executed ingress rate-limit for client-prefix and pushed TOKENIZER_MAX_BATCH=16. Early signs: CPU per-pod dropped from ~95% -> ~65% on two pods. We still saw 1 OOMKilled during rollout.
nina: Opening incident ticket INC-2619 for tracking. Customer impact: some requests returned 502/429 for ~7m window, mainly from one big client. Will add to timeline.
jordan: Assigning to sam for mitigation and nina for root cause. Handoff in 10m unless stable.
sam: Running a live heap/alloc trace on one warm pod (low-traffic) to catch the mem growth pattern. If it's unbounded memory per prompt we need a hard cap on prompt length or streaming.
maria: Heap trace shows growth correlated with very long prompt arrays (1000+ tokens) when the pre-tokenize pipeline tries to expand ephemeral structures. We'll add defensive truncation.
leo: Quick mitigation plan summary: 1) ingress rate-limit client prefix 2) reduce batch size 3) scale replicas temporarily 4) add prompt-length cap in preproc 5) roll out a memory guard (cgroup soft limit) and alert on mem growth.
jordan: Impact update: <5% of production requests errored overall; affected customers are being notified by PMs. No data exfiltration.
devops-bot: Reminder: do not exceed cluster autoscaler limit — we temporarily bumped replicas but autoscaler is at max for this pool.
sam: Implemented prompt truncation at 32k chars for preproc, pushing canary.
maria: Canary shows no OOMs for 6m, latency back to baseline for most pods. Scaling back to replicas=6 now to recover capacity.
[system] deployment/tokenizer-preproc rollout completed
nina: Root cause hypothesis: malformed client requests with extremely long prompt arrays + no upstream throttling caused prolonged CPU hotloop and memory growth; tokenization logic must be hardened.
jordan: Handoff: transferring active ownership to nina (post-mitigation RCA). Actions open: RCA writeup (nina), rate-limit rule as permanent (network team), add preproc memory guard & unit tests (eng-runtime), update monitoring to alert on preproc mem growth earlier (sre).
nina: I'll run the full RCA and post summary to #postmortems and ping product for customer comms. Closing on-call handoff now.
jordan: Thanks team — good mitigation. Marking thread as resolved-on-call, will re-open if we see recurrence. :white_check_mark:
